title: Mensural notation
description: Musical notation system used for Renaissance vocal polyphony
extract: Mensural notation is the musical notation system used for polyphonic European vocal music from the late 13th century until the early 17th century. The term "mensural" refers to the notation of precise rhythmic durations based on numerical proportions of note values. Its modern name is derived from the terminology of medieval theorists, who used terms like musica mensurata or cantus mensurabilis to refer to the rhythmically defined polyphonic music of their age, as opposed to musica plana or musica choralis, i.e., Gregorian plainchant. Mensural notation was employed principally for polyphonic vocal music, while plainchant retained the older system of neume notation throughout the period, and some instrumental music was written in various forms of instrument-specific tablature notation.
